a3065.speaker: Bar Margret Igani, CERLSI project manager ICT
a3065.speech: Said that the plan by the US Government to probe USAID activities in Nigeria and other countries is "an active step" ; "The probe aligns with CERLSI avowed belief that democracy, the rule of law and governance can only be strengthened under conditions that are transparent, accountable and which do not promote undertones of mischief in the development sector" ; "We urge government agencies, civil society organizations, and international partners in the sector within Nigeria to cooperate fully with the U.S. Mission in this critical review process" ; "This investigation presents an opportunity to rebuild and strengthen public trust and establish stronger foreign aid management policies preventing mismanagement on one hand, and strengthen Nigeria's global credibility on the other hand" ; also said that this probe will further strengthen the operations of non-governmental organizations, partners, business associates and the likes to ensure better transparency, accountability, productivity leaving little or no room for public financial mismanagement or corrupt practices of any form.

a3088.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a3088.speech: From the moment of his inauguration, announced the suspension, for a period of 90 days, of the United States development aid programme, a decision aiming to allow a reassessment of the effectiveness of the programmes in place and their alignment with the new foreign policy of the United States.

a3088.speaker: US government, through USAID
a3088.speech: On 12 August 2024, on the occasion of International Youth Day, announced the launch of a new initiative worth 25 million dollars, called USAID Mali Shifin ni Tagne (Youth and Development).

a3119.speaker: Government of Mali
a3119.speech: "Welcomes" the cancellation of USAID funding for Social Cohesion and similar programs in the Sahel region, initiated by the Department of Government Effectiveness (DOGE), and even calls for individuals to be punished.

a3119.speaker: Malian Foreign Ministry (communique)
a3119.speech: "In addition, the Malian Foreign Ministry calls on the American authorities to initiate legal proceedings against individuals who misappropriated these funds to finance international terrorism, the victims of which are Mali and other states of the Confederation of Sahel States."

a3119.speaker: Malian authorities
a3119.speech: Believe that the funds are supporting terrorism; the country's military government had suspended cooperation with USAID for several years, suspecting it of subversive work under the guise of "humanitarian activities."

a3119.speaker: Elon Musk (post on Twitter)
a3119.speech: Made a repost of the corresponding communique of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Mali on Twitter, apparently sharing the opinion of the authorities of sovereign Mali.

a3119.speaker: Republicans
a3119.speech: According to Republicans, the Sahel zone does not matter to the interests of the United States; the failures of the Biden administration in Niger caused restrained satisfaction among Republicans and gave an additional reason to criticize political opponents on the domestic circuit.

a3119.speaker: Elon Musk and his supporters
a3119.speech: According to Musk and his supporters, the situation in Niger and the Sahel as a whole is an absolute setback for the Biden administration, but not for the United States, and spending 110 million dollars on the creation of a modern air base in Agadez, financing military training programs for local military personnel and logistical support for the army of Niger is simply irrational.

a3168.speaker: Government of Kenya
a3168.speech: Kenya said on Monday it supports Morocco's plan to give the disputed region of Western Sahara autonomy under the North African kingdom's sovereignty.

a3168.speaker: Kenya-Morocco joint statement
a3168.speech: said Morocco, a leading phosphates and fertilizer producer, has agreed to immediately accelerate exports of soil nutrients to Kenya, as the two countries plan to cooperate on renewable energies, tourism, fisheries, security and cultural and religious affairs ; said Kenya also backed a Moroccan initiative offering landlocked Sahel states access to global trade through Morocco's Atlantic ports.

a3168.speaker: Nasser Bourita, Morocco's foreign minister
a3168.speech: told reporters that Kenya's position on Western Sahara, which he called "the national cause", helped add a new impetus to bilateral relations.

a3168.speaker: Musalia Mudavadi, Kenyan foreign minister
a3168.speech: said on his X account that Kenya is looking to export more tea, coffee and fresh produce to Morocco to balance its trade.

a3426.speaker: Umaro Sissoco Embalo, President of Guinea-Bissau
a3426.speech: Announced today that he had had a long telephone conversation with Russian President Vladimir Putin, in a context of strengthening diplomatic relations between Guinea-Bissau and Russia.

a3426.speaker: The Russian side (Kremlin readout of the call)
a3426.speech: Also reported the conversation, in which the two presidents expressed their willingness to strengthen the ties between their countries, agreeing to maintain a regular dialogue and to continue their personal communication.

a3717.speaker: Christopher Namagowa, Kamuzu University of Health Sciences (Kuhes) registrar (memo to staff and students, 4 February 2025)
a3717.speech: Said the stop order has led to failure to access and utilise funding for the university’s various projects and initiatives: “As a result, we must suspend all activities related to US-funded programmes, effective immediately. In the meantime, principal investigators [PIs] for US-funded programmes will ensure regular updates and guidance are provided to all affected staff and students. We understand this is a challenging time and we encourage you to reach out to your PIs with any immediate questions or concerns you may have.”

a3717.speaker: Office of the registrar, Lilongwe University of Agriculture and Natural Resources (Luanar) (memo, 3 February 2025)
a3717.speech: Said the institution had no choice but to suspend all activities: “All staff that were working in Usaid-funded projects are, therefore, advised to immediately stop working. Similarly, students that were getting support from Usaid projects are advised that their funding is no longer there; hence, may consider to either drop out or look for funding alternatives.” The memo further stated that Luanar does not have resources to continue with the Usaid-funded projects and affected students and staff must abide by what has been communicated.

a3717.speaker: Office of the registrar, Malawi University of Science and Technology (Must) (memo, 6 February 2025)
a3717.speech: Advised affected students to consider seeking funding alternatives: “Consequently, all staff involved in Usaid-funded projects are kindly requested to cease work on these activities with immediate effect. Similarly, students who were receiving financial support under the Usaid-funded projects are advised that this funding is no longer available. We encourage affected students to explore alternative funding options to continue their studies. Please note that the university does not have the resources to sustain these activities independently.” The memo said the university will be providing updates as soon as further information becomes available.

a3717.speaker: Benedicto Kondowe, Civil Society Education Coalition executive director
a3717.speech: Said the situation will have severe consequences in public universities, especially in areas of research, student funding and institutional development, and that many students, in particular those from poor backgrounds, will be forced to drop out, worsening access to higher education and deepening inequality ; “For universities, the suspension of donor-funded projects will weaken institutional capacity, limit research opportunities and reduce the quality of education. Many critical programmes that contribute to national development, including those in health, agriculture and governance, may suffer setbacks.” ; said government must apply an adaptive management strategy that ensures sustainable financing for the education sector and take decisive action to reduce corruption and promote the efficient use of domestic resources: “Strengthening accountability and transparency in public spending will not only restore donor confidence, but also enhance the resilience of Malawi’s higher education system, reducing dependency on external funding.”

a3717.speaker: Limbani Nsapato, education expert
a3717.speech: Said in the interim, government should step in to provide scholarships or loan facilities to students: “As a long-term measure, government needs to reduce dependence on donors for development projects, including in tertiary education. There is need to intensify domestic revenue mobilisation and innovative strategies such as introducing higher education levy, diaspora contributions, using idle pension funds and investing more in mining and tourism. Such methods can help increase revenue locally.”

a3717.speaker: Jessie Kabwila, Minister of Higher Education
a3717.speech: Non-response: Nation on Sunday’s efforts to speak to the minister on Friday proved futile as he did not pick our phone calls or respond to our questionnaire.

a3792.speaker: Moussa Faki Mahamat, African Union Commission Chairperson
a3792.speech: Said in a statement that as a member of the world health body, the U.S. was "crucial in shaping global WHO instruments and norms on public health security and wellbeing over the past seven decades" ; recalled that the U.S. was an "early and strong supporter" of the Africa Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, the African Union's agency for public health emergencies, which works with the WHO to address pandemics ; expressing hope that the US government will reconsider its decision, said: "Today, now more than ever, the world depends on WHO to carry out its mandate to ensure global public health security as a shared common good."

a3792.speaker: African Union
a3792.speech: On Jan. 22 urged new U.S. President Donald Trump to revisit his decision to withdraw Washington from the World Health Organisation ; expressed dismay over the withdrawal, urging the Trump administration to reconsider.

a3792.speaker: US executive order signed by President Donald Trump
a3792.speech: Cited several reasons for the withdrawal, including the WHO's "mismanagement" of the COVID-19 pandemic and other global health crises, its "failure" to implement urgently needed reforms, and its "lack of independence from undue political influence" from member states ; "China, with a population of 1.4 billion, has 300 percent of the population of the United States, yet contributes nearly 90 percent less to the WHO."

a3792.speaker: Some senior African health officials (unnamed)
a3792.speech: Have said the departure of the U.S. could also push African nations to take greater control of their health systems.

a3792.speaker: Professor Yap Boum II, deputy coordinator of the Africa CDC's mpox response unit (told RFI)
a3792.speech: Told RFI that Trump's decision was anticipated, it had been in the air, and was not surprising ; said, however, it will have a significant impact - for instance, in responding to the mpox epidemic the WHO and Africa CDC are coordinating efforts, and out of the projected funding of $1 billion, the U.S. contributes $500 million, half of the total, so this withdrawal could have substantial consequences ; "We need to consider what the US's exit from the WHO signifies. Does it imply a reduction in US support for global health? These are distinct issues. It's crucial to understand the practical implications so that we can all adapt accordingly."

a3792.speaker: Professor Yap Boum II, deputy coordinator of the Africa CDC's mpox response unit
a3792.speech: Said the impact will be considerable, depending on how the situation unfolds: "Is the WHO all there is to health? That's the key question. Could this open the door for other agencies, such as USAID or various organisations, to receive the funds. And, couldn't this also be an opportunity for African philanthropists for example to contribute more to the Africa CDC? Couldn't this lead to a reorganisation of the global health landscape? We'll get more clarity on this in the coming weeks and months."

a3820.speaker: Zouéra Hassane Haousseizé, Commissioner, head of the Central Service for the Protection of Minors and Women of the national police
a3820.speech: Announced that the Central Service for the Protection of Minors and Women of the national police carried out seizures and arrests as part of its ‘operations to combat moral depravity and juvenile delinquency’ in the city of Niamey ; specified that a total of 51,772 shisha products, devices and accessories were seized, including 13,978 shisha bottles, 17,153 shisha products, 14,622 hoses, 1,233 pipettes, 849 shisha heads, 798 pieces of charcoal, 1,477 aluminium foils, 650 shisha brushes and 950 stoppers ; added that several traders were arrested for failing to respect the article stating that it ‘is strictly forbidden to import, distribute, sell and consume shisha or hookah throughout the territory of the Niamey region’, noting that ‘at our level we have many statistics that have shown this, children are unwittingly indulging in this abusive consumption of shisha, which is harmful to their mental and physical health’ ; ‘The police services first carried out a series of awareness campaigns before conducting raids on certain places, including public squares, nightclubs, fadas and others, where these young people usually smoke, in order to seize the devices’ ; ‘traders were also arrested over the ban on the sale of shisha, and we carried out field operations where we went to the locations to seize the devices, among which were very expensive iron bottles in white and red metal’.

a3820.speaker: Zouéra Hassane Haousseizé, Commissioner, head of the Central Service for the Protection of Minors and Women of the national police
a3820.speech: Warned: ‘we intend to prosecute those who continue to bring in shisha, with heavy fines that will be paid into the treasury, and all measures will be taken for the definitive eradication of shisha use by young people in the city of Niamey’ ; welcomed that ‘one cannot fail to note a strong awakening among young smokers, the young people who were sensitized immediately stopped consuming hookah’, while warning that ‘those who have not been informed and who continue with this practice will be arrested and will answer for their actions’.

a3820.speaker: Zouéra Hassane Haousseizé, Commissioner, head of the Central Service for the Protection of Minors and Women of the national police
a3820.speech: Explained that ‘this measure comes to protect present and future generations from the physical and mental health effects linked to the consumption of these products, particularly shisha’.

a3820.speaker: Governor of the Niamey region (decree of 24 July 2024)
a3820.speech: Issued a decree banning the consumption of shisha or hookah and ordering the destruction of the products, devices and accessories.

a3820.speaker: Dr Hibe Florant, health worker
a3820.speech: Explains that ‘shisha, whose consumption is unfortunately high, even a habit among some young people or, more seriously, among adolescents, is very dangerous for human health and toxic for the organism, more precisely the lungs’ ; ‘at the respiratory level, hookah smokers may present symptoms of respiratory discomfort and chronic bronchitis, and the passing of the hose from one mouth to another can also favour the transmission of contagious diseases such as tuberculosis, hepatitis or even Covid-19’ ; ‘according to several studies, a portion of water-pipe smokers show signs of dependence which would however be less than with the cigarette’ ; ‘shisha has a more dangerous effect on the lungs than the cigarette even if many think the opposite, but after a certain study was conducted it was found that shisha is very dangerous for the organism, with effects such as the risk of lung or mouth cancer, increased expense, dependence observed in the smoker, depressive effects on at-risk persons’ ; ‘the best advice for consumers is cessation, because this practice has led several to death’.

a3820.speaker: A young shisha smoker (anonymous)
a3820.speech: Says shisha is consumed for various reasons, including entertainment, the pleasure of smoking and stress relief: ‘I find comfort in taking this product, not only does it entertain me but it is also a psychological problem because it is difficult to do without’.

a3830.speaker: Fulbright Foreign Student Program plagiarism certification (application document, 2026-27 cycle)
a3830.speech: “Some US universities and colleges have developed and published policies on the use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on applications for admission or affiliation with their institution. Some institutions may scan applications for the use of language produced by GenAI. While individual institutional policies range widely and policy responses from US universities will continue to evolve, copying language/content produced by GenAI directly into your application may negatively impact admission or affiliation decisions.”

a3830.speaker: U.S. Embassy in Mozambique (@USEmbassyMoz, post on X, March 26, 2025)
a3830.speech: “Fulbright 2026-2027 is now accepting applications from Mozambican students! Seize this chance to pursue a graduate degree or research in the USA with full scholarships! Apply by June 2, 2025.”

a3830.speaker: Fulbright Foreign Student Program (program announcement, U.S. Department of State and Institute of International Education)
a3830.speech: Announced that the program will award scholarships for a maximum of two years of advanced degree study in the United States, with successful applicants beginning their academic program in August 2026, and set out eligibility criteria, including that local employees abroad employed by the State Department/United States Agency for International Development (USAID) are ineligible for grants during the period of their employment and for one year following the termination of employment; all awards are contingent upon approval by the J. William Fulbright Scholarship Board, availability of funds, and successful academic placement.

a3922.speaker: Civil Society Coalition for Mandate Protection (CSC-MAP) and National Coalition of Civil Society Groups (NCCSG) (joint statement signed by its President, Okunola Ahmed, and Secretary, Balla Usman Aliu)
a3922.speech: Urged President Bola Tinubu-led government to stop the tradition of using armed militants to protect oil pipelines in the Niger-Delta region, warning on Wednesday that the idea of using militants may provoke another round of armed conflict and violence in the oil rich region; urged President Tinubu to be cautious in engaging Niger Delta militants in pipeline protection saying they constitute a major threat to the stability of Nigeria; urged him to focus on indigenous professional security companies in the Niger-Delta genuinely committed to the protection of oil pipelines instead of funding armed groups that constitute a threat to National Security.

a3922.speaker: Civil Society Coalition for Mandate Protection (CSC-MAP) and National Coalition of Civil Society Groups (NCCSG)
a3922.speech: Said there are widespread fears that a particular militant in the Niger Delta is using proceeds of pipeline protection to import illicit weapons into the country, and that the militant has the preconceived plan to divide Nigeria through armed conflict that would start from the Niger-Delta: "It is not right to fund armed and separatist group that has fought Nigeria and other ethnic groups in the Niger Delta. The leaders of the armed groups were once declared wanted by the Nigerian State. It is wrong to continue to provide resources for them which might empower them to import illicit weapons into Nigeria."

a3922.speaker: Civil Society Coalition for Mandate Protection (CSC-MAP) and National Coalition of Civil Society Groups (NCCSG)
a3922.speech: Alleged that a particular militant is currently involved in high calibre bribery of top government officials including some members of the National Assembly in order to perpetrate himself and sustain his armed dominion in the Niger-Delta; regretted that the militant continues to enjoy the protection of a few armed soldiers with a full truck load of soldiers; accused a former Governor of Bauchi State of collaborating with the armed militant; and alleged that the militant's sibling holds the cash portfolio on his behalf, distributing money to politicians to influence pipeline protection contracts in his favour and to cover up his crimes: "We have been informed that a militant's aide, one the militant's aides is currently in Abuja with loads of money to cover the tracks of the Niger-Delta militant. He is also offering huge sums of money to some corrupt officials of the Nigerian National Petroleum Company PLC and some corrupt people in the Presidency."

a3922.speaker: Civil Society Coalition for Mandate Protection (CSC-MAP) and National Coalition of Civil Society Groups (NCCSG)
a3922.speech: Said it is preparing a letter to the President and to all members of the National Assembly to expose the militant's crime against Nigerians and the people of the Niger Delta; called on the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) to revisit the trial of Mr Government Ekpemokpolo, alias Tompolo, and to recall the investigation opened in 2016 for various crimes ranging from corruption to terrorism; and said that instead of engaging Tompolo, the Federal Government should engage genuine representatives of the people of the Niger Delta whose lives have on several occasions been allegedly threatened and endangered by Tompolo and his armed groups.

a3922.speaker: Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC)
a3922.speech: In February 2026 declared Ekpemupolo wanted following two bench warrants issued by the Federal High Court in Lagos; he was charged with N45.9billion fraud; the EFCC had announced to the whole world that he committed offences of conspiracy, illegal diversion of the sum of N34,000.000.000 and another N11,900,000 belonging to the Nigerian Maritime Administration and Safety (NIMASA).

a3922.speaker: Justice Ibrahim Buba, Federal High Court in Lagos (court record)
a3922.speech: Had issued a bench warrant against Tompolo on January 14, 2016 after he neglected a dated January 12 summon issued to him by the Honourable Judge.

a4293.speaker: CNN (American television network)
a4293.speech: Reveals the behind-the-scenes account of the diplomatic crisis that ended with Zelensky’s expulsion from the White House; according to the American network, the American president met with his principal advisers in the Oval Office to decide what would happen next, consulting vice-president JD Vance, Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other senior officials.

a4293.speaker: White House official (anonymous), cited by CNN
a4293.speech: Said that during that meeting Trump and Vance reproached Zelensky for his lack of gratitude for American aid ; said the Ukrainian representatives protested and wished to continue the discussions, but their request was rejected.

a4293.speaker: Donald Trump, President of the United States
a4293.speech: Made the final decision that Zelensky “was not in a position to negotiate,” and ordered Rubio and his national security adviser Mike Waltz to deliver the message that Zelensky must leave the premises.

a4490.speaker: Council of Ministers (Cabinet) of the Federal Government of Somalia
a4490.speech: The Cabinet stated that Sharmarke, who currently serves as the Lead Economic Advisor to the Prime Minister and the Coordinator of the Nation Economic Roadmap, brings with him a wealth of experience having served as an economic researcher and social sector development including lead technical expert roles with the UN, World Bank, DfID, USAID, and private sector.

a4490.speaker: Office of the Somali Prime Minister (source of the report)
a4490.speech: Cited as the source of the announcement that the Council of Ministers has appointed Sharmarke Farah as Director-General of the National Bureau of Statistics and Abdirahman Omar Dahir as his deputy, and of the description of the amended Statistics Law and the NBS's mandate and priorities.

a4661.speaker: England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB)
a4661.speech: Announced Thursday that England will play a men's Test match against Zimbabwe next year, the one-off match taking place at Trent Bridge in Nottingham starting on 22 May; also announced that Lord's will stage its first women's Test in 2026 when England face India.

a4661.speaker: Richard Gould, ECB chief executive
a4661.speech: “To be welcoming Zimbabwe back for a men's Test Match will be a historic moment, more than 20 years since their last visit” ; “Test cricket is so beloved in this country, and we know that we have an important role to play in supporting developing Test cricketing nations so that this format of the game thrives long into the future.”

a4661.speaker: Claire Taylor, England women's great and chair of MCC's cricket committee
a4661.speech: “I played 15 Tests for England during my career but none of those were at Lord's” ; “So I'm delighted at this news and most importantly for the players who'll make history playing in this fixture in 2026.” ; “Young girls playing up and down the country can now aspire to play Test match cricket at the Home of Cricket. It is a clear demonstration that cricket is a game for all.”

a4840.speaker: Alassane Séidou, Minister of Health of Benin
a4840.speech: Declared 12 March 2018 as the date of the end of the Lassa fever epidemic in the departments of Alibori, Atacora, Borgou and Collines, in accordance with the International Health Regulations, which recommend observing a period of 21 days times two without any recorded case ; explained that this was the fourth Lassa viral haemorrhagic fever epidemic Benin has experienced since 2014.

a4840.speaker: Benin's national reference laboratory (certified by Nigeria's WHO-accredited laboratory)
a4840.speech: Confirmed on Saturday 13 January 2018 a case of Lassa viral haemorrhagic fever, following the recording of signs consistent with the case definition in a 35-year-old Beninese patient who had come from the village of Nadoba in Togo.

a4840.speaker: Alassane Séidou, Minister of Health of Benin
a4840.speech: Said that several interventions had been carried out both by the Beninese authorities and by technical and financial partners such as UNICEF, the Red Cross, USAID and the WHO ; reported that these interventions consisted, among other things, of activating the health crisis committee, reinforcing the local team with a joint Ministry of Health/WHO team, actively searching for cases and contacts in the community, twenty-one days of clinical follow-up of recorded contacts, social mobilisation and communication through community media, and daily coordination with the National Council for the Fight against AIDS, Tuberculosis, Malaria and Epidemics, the National Civil Protection Agency and all technical and financial partners.

a4840.speaker: Alassane Séidou, Minister of Health of Benin
a4840.speech: Offered the government's condolences to all the bereaved families and warned that the end of the epidemic does not mean the authorities will lower their guard against viral haemorrhagic fevers in general and Lassa virus disease in particular ; clarified that Benin remains, like every other country in the world, under the threat of imported cases of other haemorrhagic fevers.

a4840.speaker: Alassane Séidou, Minister of Health of Benin
a4840.speech: Invited the entire population to practise all basic hygiene measures, in particular washing hands with soap and water, and to avoid touching or eating wild animals ; added that for health personnel, observance of universal infection prevention and control measures is recommended.

a4896.speaker: Manuel Pedro, engineer of the Tsumeb Municipality
a4896.speech: told Nampa in an interview that consultations are underway with the Ministry of Rural and Urban Development in this regard. “Currently, water is priced at approximately N$8.40 per liter. We are looking to increase that amount in July 2025.” ; He explained that the new plant will improve water quality for Tsumeb residents, addressing long-standing issues such as calcium build-up in appliances, and that the facility treats underground water to reduce its hardness and eliminate clostridium.

a4896.speaker: Stella Nangolo-Imalwa, spokesperson of the Tsumeb Municipality
a4896.speech: confirmed that the revised tariffs will also account for ongoing maintenance expenses associated with the plant. “The new tariff will be determined through council meetings.”

a4902.speaker: Birhanu (Ethiopian official)
a4902.speech: “The leaders of Somalia have invited our historical enemy, forsaking the strong relationship and mutual cooperation it has established with Ethiopia,” said Birhanu.

a4902.speaker: Abiy Ahmed, Ethiopian Prime Minister
a4902.speech: Last year, he said Ethiopia’s landlocked status was a historic mistake that must be rectified – through negotiation or by force.

a4902.speaker: Western foreign policy official (anonymous)
a4902.speech: “In the international sphere, Somalia has very successfully cast Ethiopia as an outlier, a transgressor not abiding by international norms,” said a Western foreign policy official. “There’s no doubt it has the moral high ground.”

a4902.speaker: Hussein Sheikh Ali, Somali National Security Adviser
a4902.speech: Told The New Humanitarian that whether Ethiopian troops stay in Somalia “depends on how fast they get out of the MoU debacle”, adding that Ethiopia has “until sometime in October to renounce it” ; “We have tried to give them as much time as possible, but I think now it is getting closer and closer, time is ticking” ; Referring to Ethiopian troops, Ali added: “Their presence is negative. The owners of this land now feel Ethiopia is an aggressor, not a partner.”

a4902.speaker: Hussein Sheikh Ali, Somali National Security Adviser
a4902.speech: Downplayed the significance of the security pact with Egypt, casting it as similar to military support provided to Somalia by other partners such as the US, Türkiye, the EU and the Gulf states. He also dismissed speculation that Egypt could deploy troops to Somalia as “rumours”, but suggested they could be part of the new AU force. “We have not yet decided who will participate,” he said. “This is a sovereign decision of Somalia.”

a4902.speaker: Ethiopian foreign ministry
a4902.speech: In August, its foreign ministry claimed “the government of Somalia is colluding with external actors aiming to destabilise the region.”

a4902.speaker: Taye Atske-Selassie, Ethiopian Foreign Minister
a4902.speech: Said the “supply of ammunition by external forces” could “end up in the hands of terrorists”.

a4902.speaker: Ahmed Soliman, researcher at Chatham House
a4902.speech: “Egypt is fed up with the lack of progress over the GERD. They’ve walked away from the negotiating table, so they’re using this dispute with Somalia to up the pressure on Ethiopia,” said Ahmed Soliman.

a4902.speaker: Ethiopia (government position on GERD)
a4902.speech: Ethiopia says the project is vital to its economic development and argues it can benefit downstream countries by regulating the flow of the river.

a4902.speaker: Alan Boswell, Horn of Africa director at the International Crisis Group
a4902.speech: Described the security pact between Somalia and Egypt as “part theatrical and part substantive”. “I don’t think any of the military support for Somalia offered by Egypt is a game-changer yet,” said Boswell. “It’s signalling by Somalia to Ethiopia that it's unhappy. But we could also start to see Egypt invest more in Somalia.”

a4902.speaker: Alan Boswell, Horn of Africa director at the International Crisis Group
a4902.speech: “If Somalia basically orders Ethiopia out of Somalia, that would be painful for both countries... Egypt is in no way a substitute for Ethiopia. They probably wouldn’t deploy to the same areas, or possess the same expertise, if they deployed at all. Ethiopia has a lot of sway in the African Union, and there’s a big question mark over whether the AU would even approve Egypt as a troop contributing country in Somalia.”

a4902.speaker: Western diplomat (anonymous)
a4902.speech: Said that even if Somalia tells Ethiopia’s military to leave, it is unlikely to do so. “It’s very possible Ethiopia won’t participate in the new AU mission, but they could stay on unilaterally or based on an agreement with South West State, where Ethiopian troops are the region’s security guarantee.”

a4902.speaker: Ethiopian researcher (anonymous, requested anonymity owing to the topic’s sensitivity)
a4902.speech: Said the port deal with Somaliland should be understood “as a fundamentally national security action, a way of escaping a perceived encirclement by hostile states, not an economic deal”. “Abiy sees this as his historical legacy, giving Ethiopia access to the Red Sea.”

a4902.speaker: Ethiopian researcher (anonymous)
a4902.speech: Points out that Abiy has succeeded in inserting the idea of Ethiopia gaining sea access into regional policy discussions. “In this sense, his strategy has worked... He has completely changed how we talk about this issue, to his advantage. You could call that smart, you could call it dangerous, but already it's a success.”

a4953.speaker: Lieutenant Hussaini Ibrahim, Base Information Officer, NNS Beecroft (statement released on Saturday)
a4953.speech: Confirmed that the first 15 of the suspected stowaways were handed over to the Nigeria Immigration Service on Friday, December 20, 2024. The statement read: "Preliminary investigation revealed that the stowaways boarded the vessels at night and concealed themselves in the rudder compartment while attempting to illegally migrate to Europe. MT KRITI RUBY raised alarm through the Nigerian Navy Maritime Domain Awareness Facility, Falcon Eye Alignment and requested for immediate interception of the suspected stowaways." ; "The Falcon Eye Alignment successfully vectored NNS BEECROFT QRT which led to the interception of 15 suspected stowaways at Lagos fairway buoy." ; "On the other hand, the interception of the additional 4 suspects onboard MT MCC YANBU was sequel to credible intelligence availed by NNS BEECROFT personnel deployed for escort duties onboard the vessel."

a4953.speaker: Lieutenant Hussaini Ibrahim, Base Information Officer, NNS Beecroft
a4953.speech: Explained that the prompt response of the Quick Response Team has saved the stowaways from exposure to life threatening situation during the long voyage; "The effect of stowaways on maritime operations can not be overemphasized as it poses security threats to vessels and aids smuggling, piracy as well as drug and human trafficking amongst other maritime threats." ; "The NNS BEECROFT under the leadership of Chief of the Naval Staff, Vice Admiral Emmanuel Ikechukwu Ogalla, Admiralty Medal will continue to maintain credible presence along Lagos waterways and adjoining creeks to ensure a safe and secured maritime environment for socioeconomic activities to thrive." ; noted the remaining four suspected stowaways would be handed over as soon as possible.

a4977.speaker: Policy Alert (non-governmental organisation)
a4977.speech: decried the recent decline in fiscal transparency by the Akwa Ibom State Government for the first and second quarters of 2025, saying such rollback will reduce the ability for civil society, media, and stakeholders to scrutinize fiscal activities in the state and further weakens a system of checks and balances built over years.

a4977.speaker: Tijah Bolton-Akpan, Executive Director, Policy Alert
a4977.speech: reported that out of the 36 states of the federation, only Akwa Ibom, Anambra, Plateau, and Rivers have not published detailed capital expenditure reports since Q1 2025 ; "For Q1 and Q2 2025, the State has reduced its Budget Implementation Report to a 3-page summary instead of the usual comprehensive reports (averaging 46-pages) in preceding years. This superficial reporting marks a significant departure from previous transparency standards." ; "The implication is that it will reduce the ability for civil society, media, and stakeholders to scrutinize fiscal activities in the state and further weakens a system of checks and balances built. Most states publish reports exceeding 60 pages, including project-level details in key sectors like Education and Health."

a4977.speaker: Tijah Bolton-Akpan, Executive Director, Policy Alert
a4977.speech: regretted that the recent rollback in financial transparency was against the gains earlier achieved, and said: "Akwa Ibom State has over the years made steady progress in fiscal transparency and accountability. Early gains include the online publication of annual budgets (since 2015) and the publication of annual budget implementation reports (since 2018) and the holding of annual citizens budget forums since 2019." ; "Policy Alert and other civil society organisations in the state have since 2014 worked with key MDAs in the state to ensure the emplacement of legal frameworks and practices in support of fiscal transparency and accountability." ; "The state made remarkable progress on fiscal reforms in response to incentives provided by the World Bank/FG-supported SFTAS between 2018 to 2022 and the USAID State to State Activity provided".

a4977.speaker: Policy Alert (non-governmental organisation)
a4977.speech: listed key gaps in the current public finance management cycle to include lack of detailed breakdown of revenue by Administrative Classification (e.g., IGR by MDA), lack of data on revenue sources such as statutory allocations, derivation funds, VAT shares and ecological funds, and missing IGR details: taxes, licenses, royalties, fees, rents, investment income and interest earned.

a4977.speaker: Policy Alert (non-governmental organisation)
a4977.speech: reminded the Akwa Ibom State Government that its recent actions breached the Fiscal Responsibility Law (Section 48 (1)) which mandates full, timely, and wide disclosure of public finances: "The current limited reporting falls short of these legal requirements, risking non-compliance and undermining public trust".

a4977.speaker: Civil society organisations (CSOs) at the Public Finance Management Review meeting
a4977.speech: called on the Akwa Ibom State Government to "Reinstate the publishing of comprehensive quarterly and annual BIR reports including the following details: Revenue by source and classification, Expenditure by MDA and sector, Capital projects with line-item details, Align with PFM-aligned Legal Frameworks, including the following; Akwa Ibom State Fiscal Responsibility Law 2020, Public Procurement Law 2019 and the Freedom of Information Act and other relevant laws" ; called on the state government to make financial reports available online in user-friendly formats, engage civil society and media in data interpretation, establish transparent mechanisms for tracking and publishing project-level capital expenditure and regularly update and publish performance reports.

a5015.speaker: US executive order of 20 January on Reevaluating and Realigning United States Foreign Aid / USAID Notices of Suspension
a5015.speech: Following the 20 January executive order, USAID started distributing Notices of Suspension, instructing recipients to stop working on awards and not incur any new costs; emergency food assistance and administrative expenses necessary to administer it were exempted by a 90-day waiver, as was life-saving humanitarian support to several countries, while all activities related to abortions, family planning, gender or ‘DEI ideology programmes’, transgender surgeries and other non-life saving assistance are specifically excluded from the waiver.

a5015.speaker: US government (notification to PEPFAR-funded organisations)
a5015.speech: On 26 February, PEPFAR-funded HIV organisations were notified by the US government that their financial support had been terminated permanently, with immediate effect.

a5015.speaker: Modelling using the University of Denver’s International Futures forecasting platform
a5015.speech: Finds that 5.7 million more Africans would fall below the $2.15 extreme poverty income level in the next year if Trump’s administration succeeds in its aid-reduction ambition, and that by 2030 a cumulative total of almost 19 million more Africans would be considered extremely poor compared with a business-as-usual scenario, with the DRC, Ethiopia, Somalia, Niger, Uganda and Tanzania most affected; by 2030 the economy of sub-Saharan Africa will also be US$4.6 billion smaller. Modelling of increased FDI of the same volume found no evidence that it can offset the impact of the US aid reduction.

a5015.speaker: Most donors
a5015.speech: Exasperated by the apparent limited effects of aid, and concerns about corruption and dependency, most donors argue for trade, not aid, and push for private-sector engagement as an alternative.

a5084.speaker: UNESCO (list of World Heritage sites)
a5084.speech: According to a list compiled by UNESCO, Morocco, alongside Ethiopia, ranks first in Africa in terms of hosting the largest number of archaeological sites classified as World Heritage (nine sites each), followed by Tunisia and South Africa (eight sites), Egypt, Algeria, Senegal and Tanzania (seven sites), and Libya and Zimbabwe (five sites).

a5084.speaker: Moroccan websites
a5084.speech: Reported that this list includes, in addition to Morocco and Ethiopia (nine sites each), Tunisia and South Africa (eight sites), Egypt, Algeria, Senegal and Tanzania (seven sites), and Libya and Zimbabwe (five sites).

a5084.speaker: UNESCO (the UN organisation)
a5084.speech: Revealed that the African continent contains 129 archaeological sites classified as World Heritage, distributed across 37 countries.

a5224.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Ethiopian Prime Minister
a5224.speech: on his new role serving the Ethiopian Association of Civil Engineers (EACE): “There is always enough time for any job if you use proper time management. I do have a lot more time since I have resigned as Prime Minister because I am not in such a stressful environment. Now I want to spend my time implementing a vibrant, professional association which I have learned about after several years in the civil engineering field... I need to use my influence to help the association reach its full potential and take it to the next level. For instance we need to develop professional certification. The association needs to work with the government to improve rules and regulations.”

a5224.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Ethiopian Prime Minister
a5224.speech: on ethics and young engineers: “Most of the civil engineers in Ethiopia are young; so it is our duty to ensure their ethical and professional capacity is strengthened... Ethics isn’t something you catch all of a sudden it’s something that must be developed starting in childhood. Universities must play a major role in creating ethical citizens. However, the universities have very poor performance in this regard and I want to play a role in making things better... If you look at the construction industry in Ethiopia, there are some construction companies which have failed to live up to the ethical principles of the profession. The wealth of the nation did not have to be wasted because of the ethical lapses of some.”

a5224.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Ethiopian Prime Minister
a5224.speech: on international connections: “I am now engaged in various global initiatives. I have to choose from many requests which mean a very good opportunity to make our association internationally competitive. Establishing relationships with the American Civil Engineers Association and Canadian Civil Engineers Association helps us to gain prominence and establish relationships. Also, working with emerging associations in China, Europe and Africa is fundamental. Fortunately the president of European Civil Engineer Association is my classmate when I was in Finland... Sharing knowledge with associations which have a lot of experience will help us grow and prosper.”

a5224.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Ethiopian Prime Minister
a5224.speech: on financing the association and foreign aid: “I believe we have to give priority to local resource mobilization and not rely on international aid. I always look at the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church as an example. They managed to build beautiful buildings in towns. They accomplished this through the support of their congregations not resources from abroad. In the construction sector, we have good resources we have not resorted to using foreign aid. Most of the class one contractors in Ethiopia are civil engineers and they are wealthy. So if they want their profession to be respected they have to contribute... So this is the responsibility that I am planning to take with the leaders of the associations, to approach the Prime Minister and Addis Ababa Mayor to give us enough land.”

a5224.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Ethiopian Prime Minister
a5224.speech: on reducing waste in the construction sector: “There was a proclamation and regulation issued to govern the mobilization of construction for infrastructure... There is also an agency established to govern the issue named the Federal Integrated Infrastructure Development Coordinating Agency. So the government noticed the matter and even established a respective body but the problem is implementation... our culture is an agrarian culture which is transitioning into an urban culture. So there is a need to change the mindset... Many matters are going to be resolved when we join the middle-income living standards and change our life style.”

a5224.speaker: Hailemariam Dessalegn, former Ethiopian Prime Minister
a5224.speech: on corruption in the construction sector: “This is one of the major issues that always make me depressed and worrisome. The main role has to be made in society to make corruption a sin. This is not a role only to be played by the government. What the government is doing is filling the gap but other holes will erupt if this is not solved at the society level. The professional associations have to play a significant role in such a manner... If the associations are entitled to professional licensing they will regulate their members... The government is hunting the criminals but that is not a sustainable method. The sustainability has to be focused on avoiding the ethical irregularities especially corruption before it happens.”

a5261.speaker: Addis Abeba city officials
a5261.speech: Argue the edict is designed to tighten fiscal discipline as Addis Abeba shoulders the weight of its record-high 350 billion Br budget for the 2025/26 fiscal year, the first financed entirely from internal revenue without federal subsidies ; Claim that renovations to in-house facilities, public halls and office cafeterias will prove cheaper than hotel fees in the long run.

a5261.speaker: Yoseph Tale, deputy head of the Addis Abeba City Finance Bureau
a5261.speech: "We can't afford wasteful spending when our priority is investment," he told Fortune. "If their meeting rooms or cafeterias are not in good condition, they are encouraged to renovate them."

a5261.speaker: Mehariw Temesgen, public relations director, Addis Abeba City Youth & Sports Bureau
a5261.speech: "We already have alternative halls available," said Mehariw Temesgen, citing venues such as Adwa Museum and Africa Convention Centre for larger gatherings.

a5261.speaker: Zenash Ketema, deputy head of the Women, Children, & Social Affairs Bureau
a5261.speech: According to Zenash Ketema, the facility only holds 20, while typical training sessions draw upwards of 200 participants. "With this restriction, we cannot train such a large group at once in our office," Zenash told Fortune. "Since hotels are no longer an option, we'll have to depend on borrowing conference rooms from other bureaus, which will make our work more challenging. We'll be requesting exemptions for key events to avoid bottlenecks in operations."

a5261.speaker: Gadisa Girma, managing director of Haile Resorts & Hotels
a5261.speech: Called the ban overzealous. "It's reasonable to save public funds, but not by completely prohibiting hotels," he said, advocating for a calibrated policy that allows large-scale trainings and conferences to continue in hotels. "The city might save in one pocket but lose even more in another through reduced tax revenue."

a5261.speaker: Fitteh Woldesenbet (PhD), president of the Ethiopian Hotel & Tourism Employers Federation
a5261.speech: "The government is the single largest client for hotels," said Fitteh Woldesenbet, representing over 2220 hotels. "If it stops booking events, what will hotels do?" ; According to Fitteh, removing this source of revenue would not only hurt hotels but also undermine government tax collection.

a5261.speaker: Mustofa Abdella, CEO of Zafer Plus Consultancy
a5261.speech: Sees the policy as potentially self-defeating. He warned that with donor-funded programs shrinking, private demand tepid, and now government bookings halted, the city Administration's decision will compress profit margins, intensify competition for corporate clients, and potentially lead to job cuts and business closures. "This is a perfect storm," he told Fortune ; Urged the Administration to implement restrictions on the number of events city bureaus gradually hold in hotels or, at the very least, allow discounted, essential-use exceptions. "Without such measures," he cautioned, "the city risks eroding its own tax base and discouraging investment."

a5261.speaker: Atlaw Alemu (PhD), economics lecturer at Addis Abeba University
a5261.speech: "When businesses are frustrated and uncertain, they lose motivation," said Atlaw Alemu. According to him, budget targets cannot be met at the expense of private sector viability, especially in employment-rich sectors like hospitality. Atlaw called for a rebalancing of priorities, urging the city officials to invest not simply in roads and parks but also in healthcare, education, and cost-of-living relief. "People are struggling with food, not fountains," he said. "Creating sustainable jobs will expand the city's revenue base more reliably than austerity alone."

a5286.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Foreign Minister of Lesotho
a5286.speech: Described US President Donald Trump's remarks about the country as "unfortunate" and extended an invitation for him to visit; calling the statement "quite insulting," he said "I'm really shocked that my country can be referred to like that by the head of state," and added: "Lesotho is a significant and unique country, and I would be happy to invite the president, as well as the rest of the world, to visit."

a5286.speaker: Lejone Mpotjoane, Foreign Minister of Lesotho
a5286.speech: Acknowledged that US funding supports various sectors in Lesotho, including health and agriculture, and noted that while the government is working toward self-sufficiency, cuts to health aid have had a significant impact.

a5286.speaker: Donald Trump, US President
a5286.speech: Addressing the US Congress on Tuesday, dismissed Lesotho as a nation "nobody has ever heard of" while criticising US foreign aid spending, a comment made while referencing an $8 million LGBTQ+ programme in Lesotho.

a5359.speaker: IOM/DTM and NGO Rapid Response Movement Alerts
a5359.speech: Reported that between 20 and 28 July attacks by NSAGs and fear of attacks triggered the displacement of an estimated 46,667 people across Chiúre, Ancuabe and Muidumbe districts, Cabo Delgado province (IOM DTM, ETT 136).

a5359.speaker: IOM/DTM reports
a5359.speech: According to which, in Ancuabe district, the number of displaced people has risen significantly – from 155 families reported on 22 July to 444 families (1,946 individuals), with a demographic breakdown of 1,216 children, 395 men and 355 women.

a5379.speaker: United States Agency for International Development (USAID) and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC) (joint announcement)
a5379.speech: Proudly announce the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) to create the FTF Premier-Oholo (PRO) Partnership, which will combine USAID's $25.5 million Feed the Future (FTF) Premier activity and SDC's $6.7 million Oholo project; the MoU outlines a framework for collaboration and cooperation between the two agencies in addressing challenges and promoting sustainable development for the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise (MSME) sector in the region.

a5379.speaker: Ilaria Dali, SDC's Head of Cooperation
a5379.speech: "by joining forces with USAID, we aim to achieve meaningful impact and support the shared goals of economic growth and development in the region. Together with USAID, we aim to create positive change, promote sustainable development, and contribute to a better future for communities in Nacala Corridor and Cabo Delgado."

a5409.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a5409.speech: Made the case before donors at a conference in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, calling for more support for the countries of the Sahel and the Lake Chad basin (Nigeria, Niger, Chad, Cameroon, Burkina Faso and Mali); indicated that 33 million people currently need humanitarian aid and protection, including 11 million displaced people and refugees ; "The United Nations is on the ground, helping governments and communities to provide food, health care, education and shelter. But we need more support. Our humanitarian response plans are funded at about 40%," he said in a video message to participants; thanked contributors for their generosity while asking countries to redouble their efforts to fully fund the UN response plans.

a5409.speaker: Antonio Guterres, Secretary-General of the United Nations
a5409.speech: Stressed that the Sahel and Lake Chad basin regions possess immense potential, with young and dynamic populations and vast possibilities in renewable energies, but face deep challenges from violence and terrorism to the climate crisis, with floods that this year upended the lives of some five million people ; called for actions going beyond humanitarian aid by tackling the root causes of the crises: reducing poverty and inequality, particularly for women and girls; adapting to climate change; promoting peace and democracy; and urging stakeholders to end hostilities, protect civilians and guarantee unhindered humanitarian access ; concluded: "The United Nations is eager to work with communities, countries, humanitarian partners, multilateral development banks and international funds to bring about change."

a5473.speaker: Army General Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a5473.speech: Prayed for the repose of the souls of those who died, offered his condolences to their families and expressed wishes for a prompt recovery to the injured, following the tragedies that occurred at the artisanal gold-mining sites at Kokoyo, village of Danga, Kangaba Cercle, and at Bilalikoto, Kenieba Cercle ; instructed the Government to strengthen measures to prevent human and environmental tragedies in the country ; further instructed the repeal of the appointment orders of the administrative officials directly involved in the incidents (Prefect, Sub-prefects, heads of the Police, Gendarmerie and Guard, local Water and Forests, Sanitation and Pollution Control and sub-regional Geology and Mines services), the revision of certain legal texts to end settlement in the environmental field and facilitate the recovery of equipment used in artisanal gold mining for the State's assets, the suspension of artisanal mining permits granted to foreign nationals, and the launching of the procedure for the dissolution of the Communal Council of Dabia.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a5473.speech: Reported on the draft texts relating to the ratification of the Budget Support Convention including a loan, signed in Bamako on 26 February 2025 between the Government of the Republic of Mali and the Qatar Fund for Development, under which the Qatar Fund grants Mali budget support of 50 million US dollars (approximately 31 billion 447 million 500 thousand CFA francs), comprising a loan of 45 million US dollars, to support the sectors of humanitarian aid, economic development and health.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Economy and Finance of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a5473.speech: Reported on a draft ordinance amending Law No. 06-067 of 29 December 2006 establishing the General Tax Code, amending Articles 240 and 425 to adapt the General Tax Code to the new Mining Code, broadening the scope of the Special Tax on Certain Products to marble, gold ingots and other mining products, reducing its minimum rate from 5% to 3%, and extending the stamp duty on export intentions to all mining products.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali (report to the Council of Ministers)
a5473.speech: Reported on three draft decrees under the Universal Health Insurance Scheme: one setting the time limits and procedures for concluding agreements between the National Health Insurance Fund and health care providers, one approving standard management-delegation agreements, and one setting the principles of preferential pricing and the coverage rates of health care services.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals of Mali
a5473.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of Mali's participation in the "High-Level Segment" on the human rights situation, held from 24 to 26 February 2025 in Geneva, Switzerland, and of the strong messages conveyed to the Human Rights Council: the determination of the Government of Mali to implement all recommendations accepted during the Universal Periodic Review, the remarkable improvement in the overall security situation, the pooling of defence resources by the Heads of State of the Alliance of Sahel States, the ongoing drafting of the National Charter for Peace and National Reconciliation, the determination to fight impunity, the reiterated appeal to the International Community to avoid the politicisation and instrumentalisation of human rights, and the will to pursue cooperation with all human rights mechanisms in strict respect of Mali's sovereignty.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Higher Education and Scientific Research of Mali
a5473.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his mission to Timbuktu from 25 to 27 February 2025 on the operationalisation of the University of Timbuktu, noting with interest and satisfaction the evolution of the process and the effort to involve the actors concerned.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Youth and Sports, in charge of Civic Instruction and Citizen Building of Mali
a5473.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the meetings intended for students called "Citizen Masterclass," a mission of civic education, personal development and patriotic engagement aimed at making students "model and responsible citizens" and strengthening their role in the refoundation of Mali.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Agriculture of Mali
a5473.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the conclusions of his participation in the 19th edition of the National Cereals Exchange, held from 19 to 21 February 2025, which recorded the signing of 61 contracts for an overall amount of 1 billion 184 million 410 thousand CFA francs, against 261 contracts for 1 billion 70 million 988 thousand 394 CFA francs in the 2024 edition.

a5473.speaker: Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training of Mali
a5473.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the launch of the recruitment of 2,500 unemployed young graduates under the 14th contingent of the vocational training internship programme of the Agency for the Promotion of Youth Employment, with 15,021 files registered by the 22 February 2025 deadline (6,791 male, 45.22%; 8,230 female, 54.78%), and of his field mission to the Region of Gao from 27 February to 1 March 2025 to convey the message of comfort, reassurance and solidarity of the Transition Authorities and gather local priority needs.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Industry and Trade of Mali
a5473.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the holding in Mali of the 1st edition of the Africa Investment Forum of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation, themed "Unlocking Africa's investment potential," which offers the country an opportunity to promote its economic attractiveness and mobilise public and private investment.

a5473.speaker: Minister of Health and Social Development of Mali
a5473.speech: Informed the Council of Ministers of the epidemiological situation of the country, marked by an increase in the number of confirmed dengue cases compared with that of the past week.

a5473.speaker: Army General Assimi Goita, President of the Transition, Head of State of Mali
a5473.speech: Called on the population to strictly observe the measures for prevention of and the fight against dengue.

a5473.speaker: Birama Coulibaly, Secretary General of the Government of Mali (communiqué)
a5473.speech: Issued the communiqué of the Council of Ministers of Wednesday 5 March 2025, Bamako.

a5519.speaker: Moustapha Mohamed Mahamoud, Djibouti’s Minister of National Education and Vocational Training (MENFOP)
a5519.speech: In his opening address, stressed how much PRECAD strengthens, in its fourth component, MENFOP’s transformative project, namely support for the management and capacity-building of schools ; said he was convinced that this project will enable Djiboutian associations working in the education sector to collaborate better with MENFOP through awareness-raising and advocacy activities aimed at eliminating gender disparities in schools and secondary schools, especially in rural areas, support for school projects, and effective participation in the citizen project called “my own school”.

a5519.speaker: Larry André, United States Ambassador to Djibouti
a5519.speech: Emphasised the value of this project of support to Djiboutian associations in order to strengthen human capital, which is an inestimable wealth in Djibouti; this workshop is a moment of “reflection among the various actors of the socio-economic sectors in order to support human development and achieve the objectives of the Djibouti Vision 2035”, he said.

a5837.speaker: Tsotang Likotsi, DCEO Principal Investigations Officer (court petition / founding affidavit)
a5837.speech: Has petitioned the High Court to nullify his 24 April 2024 suspension and to block impending disciplinary proceedings against him. Mr Likotsi also seeks full disclosure of all evidence that DCEO Director General, Brigadier Mantso Sello, intends to use in the disciplinary proceedings. He argues that withholding this information infringes on his constitutional rights. Additionally, he challenges the composition of the disciplinary committee, alleging that its members were irregularly appointed.

a5837.speaker: Tsotang Likotsi, DCEO Principal Investigations Officer (founding affidavit)
a5837.speech: Asserts that he has always been a dedicated officer who has investigated and completed numerous cases without any accusations of misconduct - either at the National Security Service (NSS) or the Directorate on Corruption and Economic Offences (DCEO): "I have at all times operated within the DCEO's plan, implementation strategy, and policies. I have engaged in discussions with managerial leadership and investigators to align on prosecution matters."

a5837.speaker: Tsotang Likotsi, DCEO Principal Investigations Officer (founding affidavit)
a5837.speech: Challenges the allegations against him, particularly those referenced in the show cause letter, which mentions bribery, the disappearance of case files, and their alleged misplacements: "In my understanding, the DG-DCEO had concerns about the case of Rex v Motsamai, specifically regarding claims that former Principal Investigating Officer (PIO) Mathaha Motseko left a file in my custody upon her resignation and that I subsequently misplaced it. This is completely unfounded. I had no involvement with the files PIO Motseko handled. She did not report to me; she was answerable to Mr Thabiso Jobo Thibeli. There was no handover to me, nor would there have been any reason for one." ; "The case is being prosecuted by Advocate Ranthithi to my knowledge. The movement of files between investigators, litigation officers, and prosecutors is well regulated and documented by the relevant personnel. Strangely, when Mr Thibeli resigned, he handed over the files, and the first respondent (DG-DCEO, Brigadier Sello) is on record stating that he was satisfied with the handover." ; "Invariably, all charges against me relate to Rex v Lefu Manyokole and Others and Rex v Molete Selete and 4 Others."

a5837.speaker: Tsotang Likotsi, DCEO Principal Investigations Officer (founding affidavit)
a5837.speech: Maintains that he reported to Advocate Sefako Seema, the DCEO's Head of Investigations, and provided regular updates: "Adv Seema, in turn, directed me to carry out lawful instructions. The claim that I did not cooperate with assigned DCEO officers is a fabrication designed to suggest insubordination, negligence, and dereliction of duty." ; "For the record, the DCEO initiated the MCC investigation and issued its first report to determine possible prosecution. The criminal docket was then presented to the Office of the Director of Public Prosecutions (DPP), Hlalefang Motinyane, who directed the DG-DCEO to charge the accused individuals. This directive validated Adv Motelle's mandate to prosecute the case without fear, favour, or undue influence. However, she later reversed her decision, obstructing the independent functions of the DCEO."

a5837.speaker: Tsotang Likotsi, DCEO Principal Investigations Officer (founding affidavit)
a5837.speech: Argues that he should not be held accountable for cases that were not under his supervision and, therefore, has requested further particulars to substantiate his innocence: "These are serious allegations, and I expected the DG-DCEO (Sello) to clarify them before my suspension. It is a violation of the rule of law for the DG-DCEO to suspend and institute disciplinary proceedings against me over decisions made by Advocates Seema, Joala, and Ranthithi - decisions that had the approval of former DG-DCEO Knorx Molelle. This is an act of administrative overreach." ; "He (Sello) acted improperly in suspending me. This decision is manifestly unreasonable and inconsistent with the Prevention of Corruption and Economic Offences Act, as amended." ; "It is impossible to argue that refusing to furnish these particulars does not prejudice my defence. I cannot waive my right to request the discovery of relevant documents, reports, and witness lists."

a5837.speaker: Brigadier Mantso Sello, DCEO Director General
a5837.speech: Directed that detailed reports be produced on all cases handled by DCEO officers amid allegations that some officers were accepting bribes to dismiss cases.

a5837.speaker: Confidential DCEO report (compiled by fellow DCEO investigators)
a5837.speech: A confidential report seen by the Lesotho Times links Mr Likotsi and another PIO, Thabiso Thibeli, to corrupt activities. The report alleges that the duo accepted bribes in exchange for burying cases.

a5837.speaker: DCEO chargesheet (18 March 2025)
a5837.speech: Accused Mr Likotsi of "neglect of duty" for allegedly failing to complete investigations promptly, leading to the discharge of former Local Government Principal Secretary Lefu Manyokole and businessman Pitso Ntsukunyane by the Maseru Magistrates Court due to inadequate evidence in their corruption and fraud case. He was also accused of "conduct prejudicial to good order and discipline" for allegedly sabotaging investigations by recording inaccurate evidence and misplacing dockets, forcing prosecutors to withdraw cases.

a5837.speaker: Respondents (Adv Brig Sello, Chairperson of Disciplinary Enquiry, DCEO Board of Appointments and Promotions, Attorney General Rapelang Motsieloa KC)
a5837.speech: They had not filed their opposing papers when this publication went for print last night.

a5873.speaker: Centre for Global Development (Feb 2025 data)
a5873.speech: According to Centre for Global Development (Feb 2025) data, Liberia is among 26 of the poorest countries in the world and one of the eight countries where over a fifth of its assistance comes from USAID.

a5873.speaker: World Health Organization (WHO)
a5873.speech: According to the WHO, the estimated global life expectancy in 2021 was 61 years.

a5873.speaker: United Nations Human Development Index (HDI) 2023/24 report
a5873.speech: Based on the report, Liberia has a low score (0.487) and an unsatisfactory global ranking (177 of 193 countries), and is 17 of the 33 countries categorized under the lowest level of human development in the world.

a5873.speaker: Augustine Ngafuan, Minister of Finance and Development Planning of Liberia
a5873.speech: Acknowledging the impact of aid suspension, underscored the setback this development will have on the country, but also expressed confidence in Liberia's ability to adapt; was quick to emphasize that the cascading effect will impact not just USAID projects but also a wide array of initiatives implemented by local and international non-governmental organizations dependent on USAID's funds; said that organizations that have been instrumental in delivering critical services are already scaling back operations, thus jeopardizing millions of Liberians' access to healthcare, education, and other essential services.

a5873.speaker: Dambisa Moyo, economist and author of 'Dead Aid'
a5873.speech: Argued that official aid is easy money that fosters corruption and distorts economies, creating a systemic culture of dependency and economic challenges ; contends that aid has not merely failed to work in developing countries in Africa but has compounded the continent's woes, citing figures showing the exponential growth in poverty in an era of burgeoning aid - 10 percent of Africans living in poverty in the 1970s has expanded to 70 percent, while total aid to African countries since 1960 is calculated to be in excess of $2.6 trillion.

a5873.speaker: William Easterly, economist
a5873.speech: Has shown that more often than not aid tends to go to the wrong people.

a5873.speaker: Ken Opalo, Georgetown University
a5873.speech: Argued that aid both robs countries of "the chance to cultivate policy autonomy" and helps prop up and prolong the lives of otherwise unsustainable political regimes.

a5873.speaker: A renowned human rights advocate in Liberia (anonymous)
a5873.speech: "HIV aid and Foreign aid are both killers but only separated by the letter (s)."

a5873.speaker: World Bank (Oct 2024 report)
a5873.speech: The report alarms over the slow pace of poverty reduction to a near standstill, with 2020-2030 set to be a lost decade; it indicates that people living in countries undergoing or emerging from conflicts, including Liberia, appear to be particularly vulnerable to lived poverty, especially food shortages.

a5873.speaker: Afrobarometer (2013)
a5873.speech: After a decade of growth in Africa, little change in poverty at the grassroots has taken place.

a5873.speaker: China survey (February 2025)
a5873.speech: Identified new reserves in Liberia of lithium, neodymium, silver, nickel, zinc, uranium, and cobalt.

a5873.speaker: Michael McCarthy, former U.S. Ambassador to Liberia
a5873.speech: Accused Liberian lawmakers of prioritizing personal gain over essential services, leaving rural citizens destitute; accused the lawmakers of "buttering their own bread" and "feathering their own nests" while underfunding hospitals and service centres, leaving rural citizens "destitute" ; "The blocking of resources is so complete that it must be institutional: and the lack of any alarm being raised indicates a syndicate involving players at the legislature, the Ministry of Health, and the Ministry of Internal Affairs."

a5873.speaker: Global Witness (reports)
a5873.speech: Reports by Global Witness indicate that some oil blocks were auctioned for as much as $50 million in signing bonuses, but much of this wealth was siphoned off by elites.

a5873.speaker: Warner Max Corden (1984) and Alan Gelb (1988), economists
a5873.speech: In 1984, Warner Max Corden was among the first academics to attempt to explain the Dutch disease; discussions of the resource curse started in 1988 when Alan Gelb reflected on oil as a possible source of socio-economic problems, rather than an actual blessing.

a5873.speaker: Paul Rosenstein-Rodan, Polish-born economist
a5873.speech: In the 1940s called for the 'Big Push' to move what was considered then as the 'Third World' into the 'First World'.

a5873.speaker: Foreign Policy Magazine (Brief, March 21, 2025)
a5873.speech: Released a Brief buttressing the argument that the current shift in U.S. policy presents an opportunity for African countries to reset their relationship with foreign aid as well as rethink the moral and philosophical underpinnings of African development; argues that this shift is an opportunity for African nations to rethink their development models, moving toward trade and investment instead of dependency.

a5873.speaker: General Auditing Commission of Liberia (findings)
a5873.speech: Findings on President Weah's administration unearthed that monies were criminally channelled through convoluted processes and siphoned by political elites to sustain their opulent lifestyle and political career at the expense of the impoverished masses.

a5873.speaker: EMISSARY (Feb 2025)
a5873.speech: Only a tiny share of U.S. development aid goes to foreign governments; besides what is usually given to NGOs and international bodies to implement, a significant proportion is spent in the United States, supporting U.S.-based contractors and implementers.

a5873.speaker: One expert, cited in Foreign Policy (February 11, 2025)
a5873.speech: Suggests that U.S. Africa Policy should be driven by Trade, Not Aid because Washington's focus on development assistance and democracy promotion has failed, as the relationship has historically not been based on commercial engagement.

a5873.speaker: Morten Boas et al (2017)
a5873.speech: In most rural communities, traditional leaders and elderly people (men and women) usually play a 'Stranger Father' role as part of a local social institution responsible for security and social cohesion.

a5873.speaker: National Reconciliation Roadmap (Liberia)
a5873.speech: As articulated in the Roadmap, Liberians in the Diaspora have played a pivotal role throughout the history of conflict and civil war as well as since the post-war reconstruction efforts in Liberia.

a5873.speaker: Joseph Boakai, President of Liberia
a5873.speech: Iconic slogan "Think Liberia, Love Liberia, and Build Liberia."

a5873.speaker: Jimmy S. Shilue, CSO leader in Liberia and Adjunct Lecturer at the University of Liberia (author)
a5873.speech: Argues that the 90 days suspension of USAID support by the Trump Administration is a 'Big Push' for Liberia to move away from dependency and take more serious and concrete steps towards sound economic policy, improved transparency and accountability in the governance process ; "Although I do not fully agree with her arguments, it is clear that foreign aid's effectiveness in fostering development is debated" ; says foreign aid can be impactful, but only when it is used for real developmental and humanitarian purposes, or during emergency disaster situations, and is unlikely to develop a country like ours with weak accountability mechanisms ; believes Trump's policy is a radical game changer for its propensity to disrupt aid flows and compel African leaders, including in Liberia, to look inward for economic resuscitation and development ; 'Dead Aid' is not 'Dead Nation,' but an opportunity to develop a clear roadmap for governance reforms to regain international confidence.

a5938.speaker: President of the Republic, Head of State (Council of Ministers session)
a5938.speech: Observed a minute of silence in memory of the late Cocou Théophile Hounkponou, Widow Véronique Sekpon, the Honourable Siakou Sadikou, Gaston Aho, Mathieu Padonou and Sébastien Roger Ayayi d'Almeida.

a5938.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (communiqué)
a5938.speech: Adopted several draft decrees, notably on the financial statements of CeRPA Borgou-Alibori for 2008 and 2009, appointments to the boards of ONAB and FNDAJSL, session allowances at the National Institute for the Promotion of Women, three authorisations to renounce Beninese nationality, the 2012 financial statements of CeRPA-Mono/Couffo, the 2014 budgets of SONACOP, the Centre for the Promotion of Crafts and the FNDSS, transmission to the National Assembly of the Minamata Convention on Mercury for ratification, the implementing bodies of the PAURAD project, and the procedures for creating Limited Liability Companies in Benin.

a5938.speaker: Minister of Economy and Finance (communication to the Council of Ministers)
a5938.speech: Presented a communication on the implementation of the customs value certification programme, which the Council of Ministers re-examined.

a5938.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (instruction)
a5938.speech: Instructed the Ministers in charge of Finance, Development, the Maritime Economy and the Evaluation of Public Policies to launch an open international call for tenders for the recruitment of a service partner to implement the Customs Value Certification Programme within a mixed-economy company (service provider 51%, State 49%), and for the supply, installation and operation of a mobile scanner at Cotonou Port and a baggage scanner at Cotonou Airport, and to submit the results of the call for tenders to the Council of Ministers for examination.

a5938.speaker: Minister of the Environment in charge of Climate Change Management, Reforestation and the Protection of Natural and Forest Resources (report)
a5938.speech: Reported to the Council of Ministers on the progress of the programme known as “10 million souls, 10 million trees”, stating that for 2014, 15 million nursery seedlings are planned in order to obtain the 10 million seedlings foreseen, and that activities since the beginning of the year have made it possible to prepare nurseries in all the communes, with 7 million seedlings available.

a5938.speaker: Council of Ministers of Benin (instruction)
