a5938.speech: In approving the reforestation report, instructed the Minister in charge of the Environment to ensure the availability of seedlings throughout the national territory; the Minister of Economy and Finance to examine the Project's financial needs and submit a financing request to the African Union to support reforestation activities; and the Minister of Decentralisation, Local Governance, Administration and Territorial Development to integrate departmental and local authorities into the programme so as to make Benin a green country ; decided to adopt a decree instituting the planting of a tree at every happy event in a family or community.

a5938.speaker: Minister of Energy, Petroleum and Mining Research, Water and the Development of Renewable Energies (report)
a5938.speech: Reported to the Council of Ministers on the various projects of his Ministry in the field of water and energy; the Council, approving the report, instructed the Minister to continue the ongoing policy of electrification and drinking water supply in the communes.

a5938.speaker: Minister of Culture, Literacy, Crafts and Tourism (report)
a5938.speech: Reported on a working mission to the People's Republic of China on the tourism development programme for the Route des Pêches; in approving the report, the Council of Ministers decided to set up an inter-ministerial steering committee for the project.

a5938.speaker: Minister at the Presidency of the Republic in charge of the Sustainable Development Goals and the Millennium Development Goals (report)
a5938.speech: Reported on the level of achievement of the Millennium Development Goals, stating that the goals likely to be achieved before 2015 and for which Benin has taken a serious option concern MDG 2 on Education for All, MDGs 4, 5 and 6 on health, and MDG 7 on the drinking water target, while progress on MDG 1 (eradication of poverty) and MDG 3 (gender equality and empowerment of women) remains insufficient ; also reported, within the framework of “Doing Business”, on actions for the Ministry of Economy and Finance (urgent processing of direct property transfer files, improving SME access to bank credit through transposition of the UEMOA uniform law on Credit Information Bureaus, systematic electronic use of the Single Fee Slip, and electronic verification of the BESC via the SEGUB platform) and for the Ministry in charge of Energy.

a5938.speaker: Coordinator of MCA and the president of the National Anti-Corruption Authority
a5938.speech: Presented to the Council of Ministers, following the instructions of the President of the Republic, an anti-corruption action plan for the restoration of Benin's eligibility for MCC funds; in approving the plan, the Council of Ministers decided to organise a government seminar to deepen the anti-corruption strategy.

a5938.speaker: Alassane Tigri, Secretary General of the Government (communiqué)
a5938.speech: Signed the communiqué of the Council of Ministers, done at Cotonou on 19 March 2014, announcing the authorisations granted and the appointments made, including Katé Sabaï as Special Adviser to the President for agriculture and environmental protection, Jean Biokou Tossa as Technical Adviser for agriculture, Marcellin Ilougbade as President of the Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority and Djalil A. Assouma as Director General of Benin Telecom SA.

a6053.speaker: Teguest Yilma, deputy chair of the National Polio Plus Committee
a6053.speech: Stressed that Polio should be the second disease eradicated in history: “It is an extraordinary success for Ethiopia to achieve polio free status and it allows us to look ahead with great joy towards Polio endgame projects” ; “Still, we realize that now is not the time to rest, as the danger is lurking around. The status of Ethiopia as non-infected with Polio is threatened with the existence of the virus in neighboring countries like Somalia.”

a6053.speaker: Delegates from Core Group, the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation, CDC, USAID, UNICEF and WHO
a6053.speech: Addressed the attendees of the conference and reiterated the need to raise awareness against Polio and to unite communities to fight it, emphasizing the necessity to increase joint efforts from all health partners to stem the spread of polio virus.

a6053.speaker: Joint statement between UNICEF, Rotary and WHO
a6053.speech: Noted two simultaneous potential outbreaks in the Horn of Africa due to vaccine-derived poliovirus; according to the statement, outbreaks of vaccine-derived poliovirus can be stopped in the same way as wild polio by vaccinating every child: “The Governments of Somalia, Kenya and Ethiopia, as well as countries across the Horn of Africa, are committed to working together to stop the outbreaks as soon as possible.”

a6114.speaker: Marco Rubio, US Secretary of State
a6114.speech: Stated that the Knesset's moves regarding the annexation of the West Bank constitute a direct threat to the Gaza agreement; said this ahead of his trip to Israel on Thursday, where he explained that President Donald Trump had stressed that Israeli steps toward annexation of the West Bank cannot receive Washington's support at this moment, emphasising that any unilateral action of this kind would undermine American and international efforts to consolidate the peace agreement in Gaza.

a6114.speaker: Wall Street Journal
a6114.speech: Reported that the influx of American officials into Israel is aimed at ensuring the continuation of the Gaza ceasefire agreement and preventing any new escalation that could jeopardise the ongoing political efforts.

a6726.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6726.speech: In the meeting with community leaders, stressed the importance of those who live and work alongside the population as an indispensable source of knowledge about the country's real problems.

a6726.speaker: Community leaders of rural Inhambane
a6726.speech: Identified deep and varied challenges: access to drinking water as one of the communities' greatest concerns, with many families still walking kilometres daily in search of often contaminated water sources; food insecurity, with climate change reducing agricultural productivity and leaving thousands of families dependent on humanitarian aid; limited access to health services with distant medical posts; and schools with precarious infrastructure, a lack of desks and long distances travelled by children and young people.

a6726.speaker: Doctors, nurses and other health professionals (public servants at the meeting)
a6726.speech: Report that, despite devoting long hours to caring for the sick, often in precarious conditions, they do not receive due recognition, and that accumulated unpaid overtime is a cause of great frustration.

a6726.speaker: Teachers (public servants at the meeting)
a6726.speech: Highlighted the difficulties in ensuring quality teaching — constant work overload, overcrowded classes and a lack of teaching resources — and many mentioned the delay in promotions and in other administrative acts that ought to ensure stability and motivation in their careers.

a6726.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6726.speech: Acknowledged the difficulties presented by public servants and emphasised the importance of constant dialogue for building solutions that benefit not only the workers but also the users of public services.

a6726.speaker: Business people of Inhambane
a6726.speech: Described a scenario of significant losses, with vandalised shops, looted establishments and a climate of insecurity that drove away investors and customers; identified the lack of support for the recovery of their activities as one of the main concerns, and many stated that without tax incentives and accessible credit lines it is almost impossible to rebuild their businesses.

a6726.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6726.speech: Acknowledged the impact of the demonstrations on the economic fabric, reiterated the commitment to create conditions for the recovery of the private sector, and spoke of some initiatives taken by his government to finance companies and help in the recovery, considered essential for the country's growth.

a6726.speaker: Young people of Inhambane
a6726.speech: Said they felt abandoned by a system that offers no financing or training to turn dreams into reality, raising rampant unemployment, the lack of vocational training opportunities and the lack of support for entrepreneurship; several asked for concrete measures to combat crime, especially in urban areas.

a6726.speaker: Daniel Chapo, President of the Republic of Mozambique
a6726.speech: Stated that youth is the engine of the country's development and that the government will prioritise initiatives that promote training, employment and support for entrepreneurship; the head of state highlighted the resumption of the Fund to support local income- and employment-generating initiatives.

a6790.speaker: Ethiopian government
a6790.speech: Announced it has completed its military offence after taking the town of Mekele from the so called criminal group of Tigray People's Liberation Front /TPLF/, and announced that the TPLF group had attacked the North National Defense.

a6790.speaker: Sekoture Getachew, veteran TPLF politician
a6790.speech: Publicly justified the November 4th military attack against the Northern Command of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF) as an anticipatory self-defense.

a6790.speaker: Redwan Hussein, spokesperson of the state of emergency / Ethiopian government spokesman
a6790.speech: Told reporters that Ethiopia will invite others for assistance only if it feels that it failed to investigate ; “Ethiopia is led by a government which knows how to govern a nation. Ethiopia doesn't need a baby sitter.”

a6790.speaker: Redwan Hussein, spokesperson of the state of emergency / Ethiopian government spokesman
a6790.speech: Confirmed that Ethiopia's security forces shot to the air and detained United Nations staffers as they tried to reach parts of the embattled Tigray region that they were not supposed to go ; “They broke two checkpoints to drive hastily to areas where they were not supposed to go, that they were told not to go” ; “They were told in some areas they were not supposed to move. And when they were left alone they broke two checkpoints, and when they were about to break the third one, soliders shot to the air and detained them. Now, of course they are free.”

a6790.speaker: Redwan Hussein, spokesperson of the state of emergency / Ethiopian government spokesman
a6790.speech: “No entity, multilateral or unilateral, is supposed to supplant the government. We, the government, would call the shots.” ; “Humanitarian assistance must be escorted by defense forces.” ; “The government will give allowance on where to go and where not to go. There are some forces who have not surrendered. They may not have some regular leadership and command and supply of resources but they can still keep on shooting until they run out of their arms. Thus, we are saying our humanitarian assistance has to be escorted with the military.”

a6790.speaker: Redwan Hussein, spokesperson of the state of emergency / Ethiopian government spokesman
a6790.speech: “Just because we completed the operation in three weeks it doesn't mean we are in a picnic it was a very tough assignment it was completed successfully because the government was very much conscious about its people. Any life that dies during the operation is a lose to Ethiopia, but we are not hiding anybody killed by the government defense but because there was none there is no one to be accountable other than Ethiopians. It doesn't matter if they were killed by government force or TIgray forces all are Ethiopians, we are not fighting with a foreign enemy it was a family feud.”

a6790.speaker: United Nations
a6790.speech: Has openly sought unfettered and neutral access according to international principles; announced a deal with the Ethiopian government, saying it was signed on November 29, which allows aid only in areas under Ethiopian government control.

a6790.speaker: Ethiopian government
a6790.speech: Said on Tuesday that 44 truckloads of food aid had been delivered to Shire, the main town near the refugee camps.

a6790.speaker: Mitiku Kassa, Commissioner of the National Risk and Disaster Management
a6790.speech: Said the commission is working to address humanitarian assistance to 1.8 million people in the region; with the fear of the number increasing, the commission is working to do rapid assessment to capture additional number of beneficiaries, since between 22-30 percent of the urban population may need relief assistance for the short period of time.

a6885.speaker: Yoichi Oya, Japanese Ambassador to Malawi
a6885.speech: Unveilling the package on Friday in Lilongwe, said under Ticad, $1 million (K1.7 billion) will suppot Sesame export promotion while $500 000 (about K875 million) will go towards enhancing lakeside border security and regular migration into Malawi at key lakeshore points of entry in Nkhata Bay District ; “Japan remains committed to supporting Malawi’s efforts to overcome food insecurity and foster sustainable development. By addressing immediate needs and investing in agricultural export capacity, we aim to contribute to a brighter future for Malawians.”

a6885.speaker: Simon Denhere, WFP Malawi interim country director
a6885.speech: “This support reflects the strong partnership between Japan and Malawi. It will provide life-saving food assistance while also helping the country build long-term food security and economic opportunities.”

a6885.speaker: Nomagugu Ncube, IOM Malawi chief of mission (statement)
a6885.speech: In a statement, hailed the Japanese government for the support, highlighting that a well-managed migration will enhance safe, orderly and regular migration and promote increased cross-border economic activity.

a6885.speaker: Charles Kalemba, Department of Disaster Management Affairs commissioner
a6885.speech: Said government appreciates Japan’s support in strengthening its national response to food insecurity: “This timely gesture complements government’s efforts in providing much-needed relief to vulnerable communities affected by climate shocks while boosting our national food stocks.”

a6933.speaker: Tribune de Genève
a6933.speech: Reported today that thousands of jobs in the city's international sector may be at risk following Donald Trump's decision to withdraw the US' membership of key institutions, such as the World Health Organisation (WHO) and the Human Rights Commission, dismantle USAID, and suspend funding of critical programmes in organisations such as UNAIDs and the Global Fund that fights malaria, tuberculosis and HIV.

a6933.speaker: Yusuf Bangura, writer/analyst (opinion author)
a6933.speech: Argues that "what's currently unfolding poses a far bigger threat to the survival of multilateral institutions and their abilities to execute their mandates. The old order of liberal internationalism is crumbling, the international jobs market is unlikely to recover, and Geneva may be forced to adapt to new realities"; that Trump's aggressive attack on liberal internationalism means that "As long as Trump and his MAGA group are in the White House, the financing of international organisations will continue to diminish, and the liberal or humanitarian values that underpin them will be eroded," and that the international jobs market in Geneva is unlikely to recover unless emerging great powers, such as China, or the EU acting as a bloc, take up the slack - which are both very unlikely; and concludes that "Geneva may provide an interesting laboratory to study the effects of the collapse of liberal internationalism on employment and local economies... Social life in the city may not be the same after four years of Trump's presidency and European rearmament."

a6933.speaker: Yusuf Bangura, writer/analyst (opinion author)
a6933.speech: Argues on European rearmament that "European rearmament will undoubtedly lead to some scaling back in social spending, including on international aid budgets, which are often easy targets during periods of belt-tightening," that more cuts are likely in the UK and more countries are likely to follow the UK, and that "The 'guns versus butter' issue is back on the European policy debate with a vengeance"; he also argues that European leaders committed a huge strategic blunder after the Cold War by continuing to rely on the US as the guarantor of peace and security in Europe, and that Trump "has simply hastened a rupture that was bound to happen at some point, even though more thoughtful leaders would have managed the transition better."

a6933.speaker: Trump and his MAGA group
a6933.speech: No longer believe that the liberal multilateral order serves US' interests; their new policy is that the US will no longer spend money on activities or programmes that do not generate immediate material benefits to it; it will use colonial era-type tactics to leverage its power and obtain what it wants from weak states; and it will try to recoup money that it previously spent on countries, if such countries wish for its continued support.

a6933.speaker: UK government
a6933.speech: Has announced a cut in its aid budget from 0.5 per cent of GDP to 0.3 per cent of GDP (a massive 40 per cent cut) and has increased expenditure on defence.

a6933.speaker: France and Germany
a6933.speech: Have been calling for strategic independence from the US; France has offered to extend its nuclear deterrence to other European countries.

a6933.speaker: The Baltic states, Ukraine and Poland
a6933.speech: Have been vocal in their support for concerted EU military support for Ukraine.

a6933.speaker: Geneva employment office
a6933.speech: Has set up a hotline to help those who've been affected by the mass layoffs in the city's international sector.

a6960.speaker: Amartya Sen, Nobel Laureate economist
a6960.speech: Known for his theory that "people very rarely die simply because there is not enough food to go round at the time of droughts"; rather, political decisions, coupled with economic structures and social networks, aggravate food crises and famines.

a6960.speaker: World Bank's poverty report
a6960.speech: In the early 2010s, Tigray was distinctive in being one of three regions that did not see a "statistically significant" decline in poverty rates even as the country was swinging double-digit growth in GDP.

a6960.speaker: Tigray Emergency Coordination Centre
a6960.speech: Estimates that 4.5 million people - comprising two-thirds of the population - now face emergency food assistance; about half are already displaced.

a6960.speaker: Famine Early Warning Systems Network
a6960.speech: Warns "crisis" level outcomes, a designation two steps below famine, are expected; in the absence of humanitarian assistance, it can be raised to "emergency" level.

a6960.speaker: Early surveys from the UN
a6960.speech: Indicate sporadic fighting, especially in the country's rural parts, is still ongoing.

a6960.speaker: Aid agencies
a6960.speech: Have been complaining of bureaucratic hurdles in delivering humanitarian assistance to Tigray.

a6960.speaker: UN-OCHA
a6960.speech: "In some cases, partners could not travel to Tigray due to additional bureaucratic constraints at [local] levels, despite clearance received from federal authorities."

a6960.speaker: Fasika Amdesellasie (MD), Tigray region's interim Health Bureau head
a6960.speech: Wukro and Adigrat hospitals - which could have come in handy for treating malnourished people - have been looted.

a6960.speaker: Authorities in Addis Abeba and Meqelle
a6960.speech: Claim humanitarian assistance, including food and medicine, has been delivered for 1.8 million beneficiaries across the region, with plans to expand this to 2.5 million people.

a6960.speaker: Ethiopian federal government
a6960.speech: Said the state machinery was oriented after November 4, 2020 toward "an operation to save the country from disintegration"; federal authorities have since declared victory.

a6970.speaker: UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and World Food Programme (WFP) (joint semi-annual report)
a6970.speech: Said that conflicts and armed violence are responsible for most of the acute food insecurity in the regions analysed, that extreme weather is an important factor in other regions, and that economic inequality and high debt levels in many developing countries undermine governments' capacity to respond ; urged that urgent humanitarian action is needed to avert famine and death in the Gaza Strip, Sudan, South Sudan, Haiti and Mali ; warned: "In the absence of immediate humanitarian efforts and concerted international action to remedy the severe access difficulties and to reduce conflict and insecurity, hunger and the loss of human life could worsen" in these regions ; said Nigeria, Chad, Yemen, Mozambique, Myanmar, Syria and Lebanon are also in a very worrying situation.

a6970.speaker: FAO and WFP (the two agencies)
a6970.speech: Said that in the Gaza Strip the recent resurgence of hostilities between Palestinians and Israelis raises fears that the catastrophic famine scenario could become reality ; reported that more than a million people were affected by severe flooding in October in South Sudan, a chronically unstable country plagued by violence and economic stagnation ; said that in Sudan hundreds of thousands displaced by the conflict will continue to face hunger and that in South Sudan the number facing hunger and death is expected to have nearly doubled between April and July 2024 compared with 2023.

a6970.speaker: Authors of the joint FAO/WFP report
a6970.speech: Said the report focuses on the "most serious situations" and does not represent "all countries/territories recording high levels of acute food insecurity."

a6970.speaker: Authors of the joint FAO/WFP report
a6970.speech: Said the direct and indirect effects of conflicts on food insecurity are considerable and go far beyond the destruction of livestock and crops, with conflicts forcing people to flee their homes, "disrupting livelihoods and incomes, limiting access to markets and leading to price fluctuations and irregular food production and consumption."

a6970.speaker: FAO and WFP
a6970.speech: Said that in some regions extreme weather conditions caused by the possible reappearance this winter of La Nina, a natural climate phenomenon that can trigger intense rains or worsen droughts and heatwaves, could exacerbate food crises.

a7055.speaker: Nthomeng Majara, Deputy Prime Minister of Lesotho
a7055.speech: Said the state of disaster will remain in force until 30 June 2027.

a7055.speaker: Official data (Lesotho)
a7055.speech: Unemployment in Lesotho is 30%, but for young people the rate is almost 50%, according to official data.

a7055.speaker: Lesotho Disaster Management Act / the declaration
a7055.speech: The declaration, in accordance with the country's Disaster Management Act, allows the State to “take all necessary measures to minimise the effects of disasters”, among other things.

a7055.speaker: British media outlet (BBC, cited)
a7055.speech: Stressed that Trump's tariffs could be the fatal blow to the trade pact between the United States of America and Africa.

a7055.speaker: US Government (trade data)
a7055.speech: According to the US Government, the two countries traded goods worth 240 million dollars (205 million euros) in 2024, mainly in exports from Lesotho to the USA, in particular textiles and clothing.

a7055.speaker: Government of Lesotho
a7055.speech: Warned that it could lose up to 40,000 jobs if AGOA is not renewed at the end of September.

a7055.speaker: Mokhethi Shelile, Trade Minister of Lesotho
a7055.speech: Told the South African business news site Moneyweb last month that North American buyers “were not placing orders because they did not understand what was going to happen”.

a7060.speaker: Nigel Clarke, IMF Deputy Managing Director and Chair
a7060.speech: In a statement following the review, praised Somalia's reform progress despite global and domestic headwinds: "The Somali authorities have maintained reform momentum with strong performance under their Fund-supported program. The newly launched National Transformation Plan provides a welcome roadmap to build resilience, promote inclusive growth, and reduce poverty."

a7060.speaker: Nigel Clarke, IMF Deputy Managing Director and Chair
a7060.speech: Highlighted the importance of implementing the new Income Tax Law, rolling out the Pay and Grade reform, and establishing a new pension regime for civil servants.

a7060.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7060.speech: Emphasized the need for Somalia to accelerate domestic revenue mobilization, modernize its customs and tax systems, and strengthen public financial management.

a7060.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7060.speech: Commended Somalia for progress in enhancing the capacity of the Central Bank, promoting financial inclusion, and taking steps toward reintroducing the Somali Shilling under a currency board framework.

a7060.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7060.speech: Recognized the adoption of a new legal framework for the petroleum sector as a significant milestone, urging Somali authorities to ensure transparent and accountable implementation to strengthen governance and attract investment.

a7060.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7060.speech: Warned that continued donor support remains essential to sustain reform momentum and prevent setbacks, particularly as foreign aid uncertainties weigh heavily on both the economic and social outlook.

a7062.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7062.speech: Urged that the government must expand urban and rural safety nets in order to rescue citizens exposed to the high cost of living as a result of the currency exchange rate change.

a7062.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) (statement issued last Friday)
a7062.speech: Said that although the Ethiopian government is implementing the reform in accordance with what it agreed with the IMF, the government has so far not released as much money as it had pledged in order to subsidize the segments of society made vulnerable by the reform ; said that the government's plan to greatly increase the number of people receiving direct cash assistance was not carried out at the time.

a7062.speaker: The agreement document (Ethiopia-IMF programme agreement)
a7062.speech: Shows that before the exchange rate change was carried out the government had pledged to expand the safety net substantially in order to reduce this kind of vulnerability, allocating 1.5 percent of GDP in 2017 (Ethiopian calendar), of which 0.4 percent of GDP would come from its own budget for the safety net and the remainder as subsidies on consumer goods, particularly fuel, medicine and basic consumer goods.

a7062.speaker: Analysts
a7062.speech: Said that although the inflation was predicted at the time, for the IMF to speak about the problem now, after having long pushed for the exchange rate change to be made, will not be a solution.

a7062.speaker: Reports
a7062.speech: Show that the number of people who need assistance has recently increased substantially, beyond the roughly nine million people assisted each year through the safety net.

a7062.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF) assessment/review
a7062.speech: Shows that the Ethiopian government has implemented most of the matters it agreed upon while some have been delayed: the National Bank audit report deadline was extended by two months from January (Tir) to March (Megabit), and the external debt restructuring is still under negotiation with foreign creditors, with no reason given for the delay ; shows that black market pressure has declined substantially and that this has helped improve the country's foreign exchange reserves.

a7062.speaker: Analysts
a7062.speech: Say that export earnings, expected to grow substantially because of the foreign exchange change, have not performed as claimed, and that the export-to-GDP ratio is still low, which suggests that foreign creditors have delayed their decision on debt restructuring.

a7062.speaker: International Monetary Fund (IMF)
a7062.speech: Warned that if the government resorts to additional domestic borrowing and additional money supply in order to fill the budget deficit, this could worsen the cost of living and additional citizens could fall below the poverty line.

a7413.speaker: Donald Trump, US President (post on Truth Social)
a7413.speech: “South Africa is confiscating land, and treating certain classes of people VERY BADLY. The United States won’t stand for it, we will act.” ; “I will be cutting off all future funding to South Africa until a full investigation of this situation has been completed!” ; vowed to cut off funding to South Africa until an investigation on allegations that “certain classes” of people are being ill-treated by the Pretoria authorities.

a7413.speaker: Government of South Africa (statement)
a7413.speech: Said South Africa is a constitutional democracy deeply rooted in the rule of law, justice and equality and denies confiscating any land ; said it is looking forward to engaging with the Trump administration over the land reform policy and issues of bilateral interest: “We are certain that out of those engagements, we will share a better and common understanding over these matters.”

a7413.speaker: South African Presidency (statement to APA)
a7413.speech: “The recently adopted Expropriation Act is not a confiscation instrument, but a constitutionally mandated legal process that ensures public access to land in an equitable and just manner as guided by the constitution. South Africa, like the United States of America and other countries, has always had expropriation laws that balance the need for public usage of land and the protection of rights of property owners.”
